terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. `node orders.js` followed by any words shows what your reader made of them.

tasks.title: Split the words into a command, values and switches
tasks.description:
Write `readArgs(args, table)` in `src/args.js`. `args` is the list of words typed after the script's name, and `table` is a table of flags like the one in `src/flags.js`. It returns `{ command, values, flags }`.

- a word that does not start with `-` is a plain word; a lone `-` is a plain word too
- `command` is the first plain word, or `undefined` when there is none
- `values` holds the other plain words, in the order they were typed
- a flag in the table without a `value` is a switch: `--quiet` puts `quiet: true` in `flags`
- a switch with a `short` letter can be typed as `-q`, and goes in `flags` under its long name, as `quiet: true`
- flags can stand anywhere: before the command, between the values or after them
- `flags` is an empty object when no flag was given

The check calls `readArgs` with words and a table of flags of its own, for a tool of its own, and runs `node orders.js` with words of its own.
nextSteps: Run `node orders.js list orders/press-1.txt` and read the error.
Go through the words one at a time and decide for each: plain word or flag.
Keep the plain words in one list; the first of them is the command.
For a flag, find its name in the table, from `--name` or from its short letter.
hints: A loop over the words that looks at each one by itself does not care where the flags stand. Code that reads `args[0]` as the command does.
`word.startsWith('-')` tells a flag from a plain word, once a lone `-` is set aside. A short letter needs a way back to its long name: build that once from the table before the loop.

Keep `const plain = []` and `const flags = {}`. For `--name` take `word.slice(2)`, for `-q` look the letter up in a `{ q: 'quiet' }` object built from the table, and set `flags[name] = true`. At the end, `return { command: plain[0], values: plain.slice(1), flags }`.

tasks.title: Read flags that take a value
tasks.description:
Teach `readArgs` the flags whose entry in the table has a `value`.

- `--width 80` gives `width: '80'`: the value is the next word, whatever it looks like, so `--find -x` gives `find: '-x'`
- `--width=80` gives the same: the word is split at its first `=`, so `--find=ink=black` gives `find: 'ink=black'`
- a short letter works the same way: `-w 80` gives `width: '80'`
- a value stays the text that was typed, never a number
- `--` ends the flags: every word after it is a plain word, even one that starts with `-`, and `--` itself is not one of them

The check calls `readArgs` with flags that take a value in every place and every form above, with a table of its own, and runs `node orders.js` with words of its own.
nextSteps: Read "Values, and words that look like flags" in the lesson.
When the flag's entry has a `value`, take the next word as it is.
Before looking a `--` word up, split it at its first `=`.
Handle `--` before anything else in the loop.
hints: Whether a flag takes a value is in the table, not in the next word: a word that starts with `-` can be a value too.
`word.indexOf('=')` finds the first `=` only: the name is what comes before it and the value is everything after. `split('=')` cuts at every one.
Use an index loop. With `--name=value`, `flags[name] = word.slice(at + 1)`; otherwise `flags[name] = args[i + 1]` and step over it. On `--`, `plain.push(...args.slice(i + 1))` and stop the loop.

tasks.title: Say plainly what is wrong
tasks.description:
Make `readArgs` throw an `Error` with a plain message when the words cannot be read, instead of guessing.

- a flag that is not in the table: `unknown flag --colour`. The flag is named as it was typed, without a value after `=`: `--colour=red` gives `unknown flag --colour`, and `-x` gives `unknown flag -x`
- names that every object has, such as `--constructor` or `--toString`, are unknown too, unless the table has them
- a flag that takes a value, typed as the last word: `--width needs a value`, or `-w needs a value` when it was typed short
- a switch given a value with `=`: `--quiet takes no value`

`orders.js` already prints the message of an error after `orders: `, so `node orders.js list --colour` says `orders: unknown flag --colour`.

The check calls `readArgs` with mistakes of its own and compares each message, and runs `node orders.js` with an unknown flag.
nextSteps: Run `node orders.js list --colour` and see what it says today.
Read "Saying what is wrong" in the lesson.
Throw at the place where the loop looks a flag up and finds nothing.
hints: Every plain object answers to names it inherits, such as `constructor`. Asking `name in table` says yes to them.
`Object.hasOwn(table, name)` asks whether the table itself has the name. A value is missing when the flag is the last word, so there is no next word to take.

`if (!Object.hasOwn(table, name)) throw new Error(`unknown flag ${typed}`)`, where `typed` is the word up to its first `=`. When `i + 1 === args.length` for a flag that takes a value, `throw new Error(`${typed} needs a value`)`.
